summary: Multi-region sticky-session causes Idempotency header normalization and repeated function/tool calls
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate external tool/function invocations when SDK client is configured with multi-region sticky sessions and cross-region fallback. Impact: Duplicate side effects (webhook posts, downstream job creation) observed in production; customer sees duplicated invoices/log entries. Environment: Dedicated cluster, prod routing enabled for us-east primary and eu-west failover; traffic uses SDKs in Python, TypeScript, and Go.

Observed behavior: When a request is routed to primary (us-east) and then re-routed to fallback region (eu-west) mid-request (network jitter or brief GC pause), the Idempotency header is being normalized/mapped in transit which prevents server-side deduplication. Function/tool call in the generated assistant response is executed twice.

Desired behavior: Preserve idempotency semantics across routing failovers such that the platform enforces at-most-once invocation for function/tool side effects when client supplies idempotency keys.

Customer-facing impact: High - duplicate side effects in billing and third-party webhooks.
reproduction_steps: 1) Customer uses Python SDK v1.4.1 with sticky_session:true and primary region us-east, failover eu-west.
2) Send a function-calling request that includes a tool invocation and specify Idempotency-Key header in the client request metadata.
3) Simulate transient network pause (2-3s) on primary so routing falls back to eu-west mid-stream.
4) Observe that downstream webhook receives two posts with same logical id from the SDK call.
5) Repeat with TS/Go SDKs; behavior observed inconsistently across languages (TS reproduced more often).

investigation_notes: - Repro harness: used our chaos router to force failover; duplicates observed 9/10 runs pre-fix.

- Root cause: router canonicalizes HTTP header names differently when proxying between regions (lowercase in primary, Title-Case in failover path). Our server-side dedupe checks a single normalized key name (Idempotency-Key) in metadata; mismatch means second attempt looks like a fresh request.

- Language difference: TS SDK (node fetch) sends 'idempotency-key' lowercase by default; Python 'requests' usage often uses 'Idempotency-Key' Title-Case; Go net/http may vary depending on code. This inconsistency amplifies the issue under cross-region proxying that rewrites headers.

- Function-calling nuance: our function invocation lifecycle creates distinct invocation ids on each serving runtime instance, so if dedupe fails at gateway, both runtimes execute tool side-effects independently.
- Related infra ticket: INT-44102 (router header canonicalization across regions).
resolution: Short-term mitigation: Gateway hotfix copies both common header casings into a canonical metadata field 'x-rw-idempotency' before routing to serving runtime. Hotfix rolled to canary us-east 2026-03-14 08:30. Customer asked to enable sticky_session:keep-alive=false as additional mitigation while rollout completes.

SDK guidance: Documented recommended pattern in support reply — always set explicit idempotency key in request body/metadata for function calls (field name: idempotency_key) in addition to setting header. Workaround reduces exposure to header normalization bugs.
Long-term fix: Router code change to preserve original header names and normalize into canonical metadata at ingress. Planned rollout tied to INT-44102. Target patch: 2026-03-21.

SDK patches: Python v1.4.2 release adds explicit metadata plumbing for idempotency_key; TS v2.3.1 and Go v0.9.8 include helper to set idempotency_key into the request envelope. Communicated to customer with upgrade instructions.
Follow-up actions: Close monitoring for duplicates for 72 hours post full rollout; add E2E test covering cross-region failover + idempotency keys; add QA regression in CI for function-calling dedupe.
